answer: Filling 94 aliases thus needs 94 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Because the inlet index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the zenith audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a onyx index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
